\( \mathrm{X}+70 \% \mathrm{HNO}_{3} \rightarrow \mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{SO}_{4}+\mathrm{NO}_{2} \) then, \( \mathrm{X} \) can be
Which of the following are anions of class A?
questions.explanation:
• A.
    CH3COO−CH sub 3 COO raised to the negative power
    (Acetate): Reacts with concentrated
    H2SO4H sub 2 SO sub 4
    to produce volatile acetic acid vapours with a characteristic vinegar smell.
  • B.
    SO42−SO sub 4 raised to the 2 minus power
    (Sulfate): Does not evolve a volatile product with acids but is identified by a precipitation reaction in solution (e.g., forming a white precipitate of
    BaSO4BaSO sub 4
    with
    BaCl2BaCl sub 2
    solution). It is a Class B anion.
  • C.
    C2O42−C sub 2 O sub 4 raised to the 2 minus power
    (Oxalate): Reacts with concentrated
    H2SO4H sub 2 SO sub 4
    (upon heating) to produce volatile gases (
    CO2CO sub 2
    and
    COCO
    ). It is a Class A anion.
  • D.
    CrO42−CrO sub 4 raised to the 2 minus power
    (Chromate): Does not evolve a volatile product with acids but is identified by oxidation/reduction or precipitation reactions in solution. It is a Class B anion. 

Therefore,
CH3COO−CH sub 3 COO raised to the negative power
and
C2O42−C sub 2 O sub 4 raised to the 2 minus power
are anions of Class A. The correct options are A and C.

For the test of halides, the soda extract is acidified with
questions.explanation:
For testing halides, the soda extract is acidified with dilute HNO₃.

  • If we use HCl, it contains Cl⁻ → will form AgCl and give a false positive.

  • If we use H₂SO₄, it can form Ag₂SO₄ or cause side reactions.

  • Dilute HNO₃ adds NO₃⁻, which does not interfere because nitrates are always soluble.

Therefore, it is the correct acidifying agent before adding AgNO₃
